canonFrame.defaultEra: Current fifth-edition and revised fifth-edition Domains of Dread
canonFrame.editionAssumptions: Use Van Richten's Guide to Ravenloft and current Ravenloft material as the default continuity. The Domains of Dread are isolated prison-realms in the Shadowfell, each shaped around a Darklord and a particular mode of horror. Earlier connected-Core geography, political timelines, and domain histories remain valuable alternate continuity, but must not be blended silently into the current domain model.
canonFrame.timelineNotes: Ravenloft continuity has been reinterpreted across editions. Current material intentionally treats domains as mutable nightmares whose borders, histories, and even apparent geography can serve horror rather than ordinary cartography. Use a selected domain's present and avoid forcing older metaplot outcomes, rulers, or a unified Core unless the campaign explicitly chooses classic Ravenloft continuity.

campaignFoundations: The Domains of Dread are supernatural prisons shaped by the Dark Powers around Darklords.
The Mists isolate domains, manipulate travel, and can draw victims from other worlds.
Each domain expresses a specific horror logic rather than functioning only as a conventional country.
Darklords possess power and control yet remain trapped by their own desires, crimes, and failures.
Ordinary inhabitants have real lives, relationships, and agency even when their histories are manipulated by a domain.
Hope, courage, compassion, and survival are necessary contrasts to horror.
Magic works but can be altered in tone, appearance, or consequence by a domain.
The Dark Powers should remain mysterious and should not be reduced to one confirmed species or motive.
Travel between domains is exceptional, uncertain, and often requires the Mists, a Mist talisman, or narrative circumstance.
Player safety, consent, and calibrated horror are part of competent Ravenloft Game Mastering.
gameMasterGuidance: Choose the horror genre and player boundaries before choosing monsters.
Use a domain's Darklord, social order, environment, and recurring imagery to reinforce one coherent pressure.
Do not make the Darklord appear in every scene.
Let inhabitants possess motives beyond serving the domain's theme.
Use fear, guilt, isolation, temptation, and uncertainty rather than relying only on gore.
Give players meaningful choices and visible people worth protecting.
Treat escape, resistance, and partial victory as possible even when the domain persists.
Ask whether the campaign uses current isolated domains or classic Core continuity.
Mark new domains and altered histories as campaign-created.
canonBoundaries: Do not treat Barovia as the whole Ravenloft setting.
Do not silently combine current domains with the classic connected Core map.
Do not identify the Dark Powers definitively.
Do not assume a Darklord can permanently leave their domain.
Do not treat all inhabitants as soulless props.
Do not make every Vistani character a fortune-teller, criminal, or servant of Strahd.
Do not use mental illness, disability, ethnicity, or queerness as automatic horror.
Do not remove player agency through fear mechanics or coercive themes without agreement.
Do not assume published adventure outcomes have occurred.
Do not confuse a domain's false or mutable history with objective multiversal history.

referenceChunks.title: Domains, Darklords, and the Dark Powers
referenceChunks.editionScope: Van Richten's Guide to Ravenloft and later current material
referenceChunks.text: The Domains of Dread are isolated demiplanes within the Shadowfell. Each domain functions as a supernatural prison centered on a Darklord, usually a powerful person whose choices, crimes, obsessions, or refusal to change made them suitable for torment. The Darklord may rule openly, manipulate institutions, haunt the wilderness, or remain hidden, but the domain repeatedly denies what they most desire. The Dark Powers created or maintain these prisons, yet their identity and purpose are deliberately uncertain. They may judge, feed, experiment, reflect evil, or pursue motives mortals cannot know. Do not make them a pantheon with clear statistics or routine conversation. A Darklord has influence over the domain and can often close its borders, but is not free. Their victories reproduce the conditions of punishment. Strahd can dominate Barovia but cannot obtain the love and vindication he believes he deserves. Other Darklords face different cycles. Domains can contain fabricated histories, recurring people, altered memories, or inhabitants drawn from elsewhere. This does not make suffering unreal. Treat inhabitants as people whose lives matter, not scenery generated for the Darklord. The domain's horror should emerge from its structure. Law, weather, landscape, religion, economy, and social roles reinforce the prison. A Darklord does not need to order every misfortune. Institutions and frightened people can perpetuate the pattern. The player characters are not automatically prisoners for moral wrongdoing. They may be drawn by the Mists, born in a domain, enter deliberately, or become involved through another world. Their choices can save lives and change local conditions even when the Dark Powers remain.

referenceChunks.title: The Mists and Travel Between Domains
referenceChunks.text: The Mists surround and separate the Domains of Dread. They can appear in roads, forests, seas, buildings, dreams, or other worlds, swallowing travelers and depositing them where the Dark Powers or story require. Ordinary maps do not create reliable routes between domains. A Mist talisman is an object linked to a destination, such as local soil, a distinctive coin, written token, relic, or symbolic item. It can help guide a traveler through the Mists, though success is never equivalent to scheduled public transport. Vistani travelers and other specialists may know routes, rituals, or Mistways. Darklords can close domain borders. The manifestation differs by domain: choking fog, endless roads, supernatural storms, walls of undead, psychic barriers, or another horror consistent with the realm. The closure usually prevents escape rather than every internal journey. Older Ravenloft material described a connected Core, clusters, islands, and relatively stable Mistways. That is a valid classic continuity but not the default current map. If a campaign uses it, load a separate geographic overlay. Travel should create uncertainty without becoming arbitrary punishment. Provide clues, talismans, guides, costs, and choices. The Mists can separate allies, distort time, or deliver a traveler to an unintended domain, but frequent untelegraphed relocation can destroy planning. People within a domain may know only local geography and rumors of other lands. Merchants, sailors, scholars, and Vistani can possess wider knowledge. A Barovian peasant need not understand the Shadowfell or believe another domain exists.

referenceChunks.title: Horror Structure and Player Safety
referenceChunks.text: Ravenloft supports gothic horror, body horror, cosmic horror, folk horror, ghost stories, psychological horror, dark fantasy, disaster horror, and other modes. A campaign should select themes deliberately rather than piling every disturbing image into one domain. Horror works through anticipation, uncertainty, vulnerability, consequence, and attachment. Establish ordinary routines and people before threatening them. A closed inn, missing child, altered portrait, failed harvest, or law that everyone fears can be more effective than constant graphic violence. Player consent and safety tools are practical Game Mastering, not an interruption of mood. Discuss lines, veils, phobias, harm to children, sexual violence, body horror, loss of control, and other likely themes. Provide a way to pause or redirect content without requiring public explanation. Fear and stress mechanics should create choices, not force a player to perform unwanted behavior or lose control of a character for long periods. Describe sensory and emotional pressure while leaving room for the player to decide how courage appears. Ravenloft should not equate mental illness, disability, disfigurement, or marginalized identity with evil. A villain can be obsessive, cruel, or deluded without turning a diagnosis into the monster. Avoid cultural caricature, especially in older material whose depictions require revision. Hope sharpens horror. Communities can care for one another, victims can resist, and monsters can be understood without being excused. Even a tragic ending should follow meaningful decisions rather than the assumption that nothing matters in Ravenloft.

referenceChunks.title: Magic, Faith, and Death in the Domains
referenceChunks.text: Magic functions within the Domains of Dread, but the setting can alter its appearance, emotional texture, and consequence. Divination may produce symbolic or incomplete answers. Summoning can draw beings through barriers without guaranteeing return. Teleportation and planar travel cannot simply bypass closed borders or the Mists. Divine magic remains available even when a cleric cannot contact a deity directly. Priests interpret this through faith, local doctrine, or the possibility that the Dark Powers imitate a response. The Game Master should not use that uncertainty to invalidate a player's class. Resurrection can be difficult, unwanted, or changed by the domain. A returned person may carry a haunting, altered memory, or attention from something in the Mists. Such consequences should be established with player consent and should not make every healing spell secretly malicious. Undead are common in several domains, but their nature varies. Ghosts may be bound by unfinished acts, vampires by hunger and control, revenants by purpose, and mindless dead by curse or magic. Do not use one universal explanation. Souls are a complicated topic. Some Ravenloft stories include people without conventional souls, reincarnation, trapped spirits, and fabricated histories. Treat such lore carefully. An inhabitant's emotions and moral worth are not invalidated by metaphysical uncertainty. Magic should reinforce a domain's genre. In Lamordia it may be framed through scientific arrogance; in Har'Akir through tombs and divine rites; in Barovia through curses, old faiths, and vampiric rule. Mechanics remain those of the selected ruleset unless a domain rule clearly changes them.

referenceChunks.title: Barovia and Count Strahd von Zarovich
referenceChunks.editionScope: Curse of Strahd and current Ravenloft
referenceChunks.text: Barovia is a valley enclosed by mountains and Mists, dominated by Castle Ravenloft and Count Strahd von Zarovich. Strahd was a conqueror and noble who murdered his brother Sergei and pursued Tatyana, whose love he believed he deserved. His pact, transformation into a vampire, and refusal to accept responsibility define his imprisonment. Tatyana's soul repeatedly returns in new lives, while Strahd attempts to possess or control her. The cycle is abuse, not tragic romance. Her reincarnations are people with agency, not prizes in a contest between men. The village of Barovia lies beneath the castle's shadow. Vallaki is a larger settlement shaped by authoritarian attempts to enforce happiness and deny fear. Krezk, the Abbey of Saint Markovia, the Amber Temple, Berez, and other sites create distinct local pressures. Exact conditions may depend on whether Curse of Strahd is occurring. Strahd controls weather, spies, servants, borders, and much of the valley's political fear, but he is not omniscient. Barovians survive through family, trade, faith, resignation, rebellion, and accommodation. The Vistani have important connections to travel and Strahd, yet they are not one loyal criminal faction. Use named individuals, families, goals, and disagreements. Avoid older stereotypes. Do not assume a published group has defeated Strahd or that every Barovia campaign must follow the adventure's sequence. The domain can support political resistance, village survival, investigation, rescue, and stories about breaking smaller cycles of control.

referenceChunks.title: Darkon and the Memory of Azalin
referenceChunks.text: Darkon was long ruled by Azalin Rex, a lich and powerful wizard who resented the limits of his domain and repeatedly sought escape. In the current presentation, Azalin has disappeared and Darkon is coming apart. Regions can be consumed by the Mists, while factions and would-be rulers struggle over what remains. Darkon historically imposed identity through supernatural memory. New arrivals could acquire false personal histories and believe they had always belonged. This makes records, ancestry, and truth central themes. Inhabitants are not merely confused props; they have relationships and institutions built from memories that may be metaphysically unstable. The domain includes cities, haunted lands, magical learning, undead influence, and fragments with different rulers or dangers. Current canon encourages the Game Master to decide what happened to Azalin and whether his disappearance was escape, transformation, failure, or a scheme. Do not restore a stable classic Darkon automatically. Its disintegration is the current operating pressure. Factions may seek a monarch, preserve communities, exploit refugees, investigate reality, or accelerate collapse. Darkon supports campaigns about memory, national identity, magical ambition, and disaster. A census can become a weapon. A family archive can prove that a town did not exist last year. A local ruler may genuinely protect people while building a new tyranny. Keep Azalin's exact fate unresolved unless the campaign chooses an answer. The domain's horror is not only a lich's cruelty but the possibility that home, history, and self can be rewritten.

referenceChunks.title: Lamordia and Scientific Horror
referenceChunks.text: Lamordia is a cold domain of scientific ambition, industrial hardship, body modification, social inequality, and attempts to conquer death. In the current continuity, Dr. Viktra Mordenheim is the Darklord. Her experiments and obsession with Elise drive a cycle of control, rejection, and escalating violation. The domain's settlements depend on mining, manufacture, medicine, and survival in a harsh climate. Wealthy patrons and scientists can pursue extraordinary research while workers and experimental subjects bear the cost. Flesh golems, reanimated bodies, prosthetics, alchemy, and engineered life appear through a language of science that may still be magical in D&D terms. Scientific horror should focus on ethics, consent, class, and arrogance rather than treating medicine, disability, or prosthetics as inherently monstrous. A compassionate surgeon, disabled inventor, or constructed person can oppose Mordenheim's worldview. Elise is not merely an object whose body justifies the Darklord's actions. Give her goals, fear, anger, and choices. Other created beings likewise deserve individual treatment. Weather, isolation, damaged infrastructure, laboratories, universities, hospitals, and industrial patrons create adventures beyond the Darklord's central relationship. A town may depend on a process known to be harmful. A researcher can discover that a respected mentor falsified consent. Older Ravenloft continuity used Victor Mordenheim and different details. Do not combine the two Darklords or histories unless the campaign deliberately creates a hybrid.

referenceChunks.title: Dementlieu and Borca
referenceChunks.text: Dementlieu is a domain of social performance, false status, masquerade, and fear of exposure. Darklord Saidra d'Honaire presides over elite society and punishes those she judges fraudulent, while her own identity and claims are built on deception. Port-a-Lucine's balls, salons, fashions, artists, servants, and poor districts all participate in a hierarchy where appearance can become life or death. The horror is not that poor people imitate wealth. It is that a ruling culture defines human value through exclusion and punishes people for surviving within its rules. Investigations can concern forged identities, disappeared servants, patronage, art, debt, and supernatural judgment. Borca is a domain of poison, family power, political intrigue, and intimate betrayal. Its Darklords, Ivana Boritsi and Ivan Dilisnya, control rival estates and networks while remaining trapped in relationships of suspicion, cruelty, and dependency. Nobles, merchants, servants, apothecaries, spies, and villagers navigate layered patronage. Poison in Borca is social as well as chemical. A marriage contract, gift, medical treatment, invitation, or rumor can be an attack. Institutions survive because people need them even when their leaders are dangerous. Both domains support noncombat play where etiquette, evidence, and alliances matter. Do not make every noble secretly supernatural or every servant helpless. Resistance can use gossip, kitchens, ledgers, theater, medicine, and solidarity.

referenceChunks.title: Falkovnia and Kalakeri
referenceChunks.text: Current Falkovnia is a domain of disaster horror. Darklord Vladeska Drakov maintains military rule while recurring waves of undead assault the surviving population. Her obsession with control, martial glory, and refusal to change consumes the people whose survival she claims to protect. The domain supports siege, evacuation, scarcity, military law, triage, refugee movement, and the question of whether preserving the regime is the same as preserving lives. The undead attacks are terrible, but human decisions determine who receives food, shelter, and protection. This current Falkovnia differs sharply from classic continuity, where another Vlad Drakov ruled a militarized state with different themes. Do not combine rulers or histories by accident. Kalakeri is a domain of political and familial horror shaped by a struggle among royal siblings. Ramya Vasavadan, a deathless ruler, seeks to reclaim or maintain power amid betrayal, rebellion, and the consequences of her own rule. Arijani and Reeva pursue competing claims and alliances. Kalakeri's horror involves legitimacy, caste and class pressure, colonial interpretations, family grievance, war, and supernatural transformation. Treat its culture as more than a backdrop for palace violence. Villages, temples, soldiers, merchants, and displaced people have stakes in the succession. In both domains, military conflict should not erase civilian agency. Characters can negotiate corridors, preserve records, expose commanders, protect food, or decide which claimant can be constrained rather than merely choosing a flag.

referenceChunks.title: Tepest, Kartakass, and Folk Horror
referenceChunks.text: Tepest is a domain of folk horror, scarcity, sacrifice, and fear of the fey. Mother Lorinda is a hag and Darklord whose desires and bargains shape local life. Communities may uphold rituals and accusations because they believe terrible alternatives will follow. The horror works when villagers possess reasons, disagreements, and memories rather than existing as irrational mobs. Fey beings in Tepest should be uncanny, beautiful, dangerous, and bound by unfamiliar rules. Not every fey is an agent of the Darklord. A local custom may protect people while another serves exploitation. Kartakass is a domain of performance, ambition, predation, and stories that consume their tellers. Harkon Lukas is a charismatic wolfwere Darklord whose desire for admiration and legacy traps him in repeated failure. Music, taverns, rival performers, wilderness, and communal storytelling are central. Performers in Kartakass can gain status while becoming vulnerable to patrons, rivals, supernatural audiences, and their own constructed personas. The domain should not become one musical joke or endless werewolf attack. Folk horror depends on relationships to land, tradition, authority, and outsiders. Avoid treating rural people as stupid. A custom can contain practical knowledge whose original explanation was lost. Outsiders can misread a danger, and reformers can discover that changing a ritual requires replacing the protection it provided.

referenceChunks.title: Bluetspur, Har'Akir, and Valachan
referenceChunks.text: Bluetspur is a domain of cosmic and psychological horror dominated by a dying elder brain often called the God-Brain. Mind flayers, alien experiments, fractured memory, impossible landscapes, and uncertainty over whether an event occurred physically or mentally define the domain. Use memory loss carefully. Give players clues, consent, and ways to reconstruct events. Do not erase character history merely to manufacture surprise. The God-Brain should remain vast and indirect rather than a routine boss encounter. Har'Akir is a desert domain centered on ancient tombs, divine authority, social order, and the Darklord Ankhtepot. His desire to escape mortality and divine punishment shaped his curse. The domain contains living communities, priests, workers, traders, and rulers, not only mummies and pyramids. Water, burial, labor, and competing religious claims create grounded stories. Valachan is a dangerous wilderness domain ruled by Chakuna, who replaced the former Darklord by taking on the domain's terrible bargain. The domain's hunt, predation, and survival pressures raise questions about whether maintaining the prison requires repeating violence. Wilderness horror should not portray local people as primitive or the landscape as evil emptiness. Communities possess expertise, routes, and reasons to remain. Monsters, weather, hunting laws, and the Darklord's cycle threaten that life. These domains require distinct tone. Bluetspur destabilizes knowledge, Har'Akir binds history and death to power, and Valachan turns pursuit and ecology into moral pressure.

referenceChunks.title: Mordent, the Sea, and Traveling Domains
referenceChunks.text: Mordent is associated with ghost stories, old estates, coastal fog, inheritance, spiritualism, and the work of monster hunters. Its history includes the Weathermay-Foxgrove family and Rudolph van Richten's legacy, but local life should not revolve only around famous investigators. Ghosts in Mordent often emerge from family secrets, betrayal, unacknowledged death, and places that preserve emotional residue. An investigation can resolve one haunting without cleansing the whole domain. The Sea of Sorrows and other Mist-bound waters contain islands, ships, ports, monsters, and domains whose routes change. Naval travel through the Mists should require navigational knowledge and narrative choices rather than a stable ocean chart. The Carnival is a traveling domain and community connected to Isolde, performers, outsiders, and a dangerous pursuit. It can provide refuge and wonder while carrying its own tensions. Treat carnival members as people rather than a display of bodies. Cyre 1313, the Mourning Rail, is a train-like domain associated with passengers fleeing catastrophe, denial, and a journey that never safely arrives. It connects Ravenloft horror to Eberron imagery without making the entire Eberron setting part of Ravenloft. Traveling domains are useful connective tissue, but should not become safe buses between realms. Their communities have rules, needs, and dangers. Arrival can offer respite while advancing a different kind of horror.

referenceChunks.title: Monster Hunters and Organizations
referenceChunks.text: Rudolph van Richten is a famous monster hunter whose scholarship, victories, failures, prejudices, and personal losses shaped later hunters. He should be treated as a fallible figure, not an omniscient narrator. Ez d'Avenir is an accomplished hunter with her own methods, history, and agency, not merely his apprentice. The Weathermay-Foxgrove twins, Keepers of the Feather, Order of the Guardians, priests, local protectors, scholars, and survivor networks represent other forms of resistance. Organizations rarely possess complete information across domains. A monster hunter needs research, allies, safehouses, equipment, trust, and local permission. Knowledge from one domain may fail in another because curses and metaphysics differ. Books can contain errors or dangerous omissions. Hunters can become harmful when they treat suspected people as monsters, value secrecy over lives, or reproduce old prejudice. A campaign should distinguish necessary caution from persecution. Player characters should develop their own expertise rather than receiving a complete dossier from a famous NPC. Give clues through witnesses, folklore, physical evidence, dreams, records, and failed prior attempts. Let preparation create advantages without removing uncertainty. Survival networks are especially important. An innkeeper who hides refugees, a doctor who recognizes a curse, or a ferryman who knows a Mist sign can be as valuable as a legendary hunter.

referenceChunks.title: Classic Ravenloft Continuity
referenceChunks.text: Classic Ravenloft often presents a geographic Core in which several domains share borders, with clusters and islands elsewhere in the Mists. Trade, diplomacy, war, roads, and migration can operate more like relations among neighboring countries. Darklords still remain imprisoned, and borders can close supernaturally. This continuity includes versions of domains and Darklords that differ from current material. Falkovnia, Lamordia, Dementlieu, Darkon, and others may have different rulers, histories, populations, and themes. Major metaplot events such as the Grand Conjunction and Grim Harvest alter the classic timeline. Use classic sourcebooks when a campaign wants long-term political geography, detailed local history, and the older setting structure. Do not lift one classic ruler into a current domain while retaining the current history unless the hybrid is intentional. Vistani depiction in older works often relies on harmful stereotypes. Preserve their importance to Mist travel and Ravenloft history while using current, individualized characterization. A classic campaign should choose a date because domains can appear, vanish, merge, or change. A current campaign can borrow a town, family, or institution from classic lore, but mark the adaptation as campaign-created if no current source establishes it. The two continuities are toolkits, not a puzzle that must be reconciled into one objective timeline. Ravenloft's Mists permit alternate versions, but the Game Master should still tell the AI which model governs the campaign.

referenceChunks.title: Common Ravenloft Canon Traps
referenceChunks.text: The largest canon trap is mixing current isolated domains with classic Core geography. Choose a continuity before establishing borders, rulers, or metaplot. Barovia is one domain, not the setting. Strahd is not every Darklord's superior. The Dark Powers have no confirmed single identity or moral program. Darklords possess authority but remain prisoners. Do not make every inhabitant a fabricated soulless prop. Do not use the Mists to negate every plan. Do not assume a published adventure was completed. Vistani are a diverse people, not a supernatural service class, criminal stereotype, or collective servant of Strahd. Current material should guide their portrayal. Horror does not excuse removing player consent or agency. Avoid treating disability, mental illness, ethnicity, gender, or sexuality as the source of monstrosity. Revise harmful older material rather than reproducing it for authenticity. Magic cannot normally escape closed domains, but it should still allow characters to use their abilities. Fear should produce decisions, not arbitrary control. When uncertain about a domain's mutable history, describe what inhabitants believe and identify the source frame. A coherent, chosen nightmare is better than a catalogue of contradictory lore.
